correctness.rationale: The convex digitwise objective has its exact maximum at the upper digit for every i<j_r. For each j-th digit a this bound is simultaneously attained at (a+1)j_r!-1. The definition of a_r excludes all higher blocks; the inspected JIS Theorem 1 proves descent above (j_r+1)!, covering the remaining infinite range. The a_r endpoint is a concrete failure. Independent exact-digit computations check all r=2..40 block identities and exhaustive below-old-bound cases r=2..6.

originality.rationale: The published universal theorem establishes descent at and above (j_r+1)!, while the new theorem gives the exact smaller cutoff and explicit last-failure witness for every exponent. Source sections were compared at statement-and-implication level; no matching prior theorem was identified in the actual searches. An unindexed equivalent remains possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed independent solution or implicit optimization in other works might overlap.
The new proof relies on the correctness of the published high-range theorem; its statement and proof were inspected, not independently re-proved in full.

value.rationale: The least universal one-step descent threshold is a natural trapping-set boundary used to reduce factoradic happy dynamics to finite analysis. The theorem gives its exact value for all exponents, with sharp last-failure witnesses and cases where the older sufficient bound overestimates by factors. This is more than a sample numeric adjustment and does not claim to classify cycles.
